Chattanooga–It hasn’t been that long–less than a month–since Jesse Elison spoke to an industry event and addressed the issue of the beleaguered new Motus registration system.
The deputy administrator of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) spoke Monday at FreightWaves’ Broker Compliance Symposium, one of two one-day sessions that serve as a prelude to the larger Future of Freight Festival here that begins Tuesday
The biggest news in his presentation was really no news: after saying at the National Motor Freight Traffic Association in early October that FMCSA was “weeks away” from fixing the issues with the rollout of the agency’s new registration system, Elison offered no new indication that a resolution was at hand.
Interviewed by FreightWaves podcast host Charles Gracey, Elison did say it would be “really weeks and not months, not like six months before we tackle this, before we stabilize it.” He conceded that the “user experience” has been on “working on keeping people out,” which is actually a goal, to ensure that unqualified carriers can not register with the system. “But it is still absolutely more people than just the bad actors we intended it for,” Elison said.
Keeping out some bad guys
“But that measuring stick, it has worked,” Elison said about the blocked path for unqualified registrants. “But we need to be a little better than that. There are companies out there that want to operate. They want to build this trust.”
Elison added that conditions are still better than the first four to six weeks of Motus’ operations, “which were really, really brutal.”
“You’re trying to fix something and then you break it, and then you need to get your handle around that where you’re not breaking things and you’re going in the right direction,” Elison said.
Elison spoke of the long-term benefits of Motus without any indication that conditions for its users will be better soon. “Motus is going to deliver,” Elison said. “It’s going to be the system that really serves the industry.”
Users who are experiencing “challenges” should “reach out to us,” Elison said. “Please contact us because we move on those in real time.”
FMCSA has waived certain registration requirements as a result of the Motus woes. Elison’s message at the symposium: “If you don’t need to go in, don’t go in yet.”
For those who do have immediate registration needs, Elison recommended that if they can’t fully register, “reach out to your insurance contacts. Reach out to whoever you have to. Reach out directly to FMCSA and we will definitely reach out to them.”
Changes due to elections?
There is little doubt that FMCSA and the Department of Transportation under Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy and FMCSA administrator Derek Barrs have shaken up trucking regulation like no other pair of top guns have done in years. Whether it’s the move to restrict non-domiciled holders of CDLs or shutting down CDL schools , the impact has been significant.
Motus was an inherited project, but neither Elison nor Barrs has blamed earlier administrators for its problems.
With a Republican defeat of some magnitude projected for Election Day next week, Elison said he did not see a change in current FMCSA policies.
“Regardless of how things go over in the next week or so, we are going to continue to deliver, and we’ve got the support from the Secretary, which is an absolute game changer,” Elison said.
He added that there “will be a little bit of wind maybe attempted to take that out of our sail.”
Broker transparency rule…it’s coming
One looming issue: the broker transparency rule . Whatever is in the final rule is not known, but it will govern to some degree what brokers must disclose to shippers and carriers about their own activities. Its release has been seen as somewhat close to imminent for awhile.
Elison would only say that “you’re going to hear a lot more (FMCSA actions) like the broker transparency rule.” It will be part of what Elison said would be other rules that FMCSA “is going to deliver on in the very near future.”
One issue Elison said FMCSA will seek to deliver on “in the near future” is in the agency’s Unified Agenda, released over the summer, a sort of formal “to-do” list, is for changes or strengthening of rules governing new entrants. Elison described it as a priority.
In the Unified Agenda , FMCSA said it would seek a formal rulemaking “for ensuring a new applicant carrier is knowledgeable about the applicable safety requirements before being granted New Entrant authority.”
FMCSA, according to the Unified Agenda, “is considering whether to implement a proficiency examination as part of its revised New Entrant Safety Assurance Process as well as other alternatives.”
Part of the agency’s efforts in that regard would be to push back against allowing CDL schools to self-certify their compliance with federal rules. Elison said a goal would be to “bring uniformity across the board.”

This Inconspicuous DIY Camper Van Looks Like Any Other Van — Until You Step Inside
22 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Amy Camps
Camper vans done by specialized companies show us just how good a camper van can be. However, it's DIY projects that inspire us the most, showing us that creating a home on wheels by yourself is not an impossible task. That's the type of build I'd like to share with you today.
What we have here is a conversion based on a 2020 Citroen Relay with a medium wheelbase. It was crafted by Amy, who's known online as Amy Camper, over the course of the last 2.5 years.
On the outside, the Relay looks like a standard van, with few indicators that it's actually a home on wheels. The only notable mods are a boiler exhaust vent, a shore power connection, a water inlet, and two 170 W solar panels on the roof - all these will go unnoticed for most people. Amy also painted the front bumper white and the wheels black.
Stepping inside, a warm, beautifully designed interior will greet you. Regarding aesthetics, Amy opted for cabinetry covered in a cream vinyl wrap, walls finished in the same color, and wood-imitating laminate flooring with a carpet on top. The look is complemented by gold accents, such as the handles for the cabinets and drawers, and some pine elements, like a door frame or the headliner shelf.
The interior has a closed layout, with a wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, this wall has two sliding doors that allow you to pass from one area to another or close them off, as needed. Amy can also keep them open and use a curtain for more privacy.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Amy Camps If you leave the door open, you can swivel the passenger seat around to face the back of the van, and attach a Lagun table to the B-pillar by the seat. Just to be clear, this is a right-hand-drive van, so the passenger side is the vehicle's left side.
Straight ahead as you enter, you'll come across the kitchen. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a cover, a two-burner LPG-powered stovetop, a pine butcher block countertop, and a 50-liter fridge with a freezer compartment.
A vent fan above will help draw out the smells and fumes from cooking. Moreover, you have a window behind the kitchen, perfectly positioned to enjoy the surrounding views while preparing a meal.
Two overhead cabinets, a small shelf with a lip, a slide-out bin, and four drawers are available for storage in the kitchen.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Amy Camps Next, we have the seating area split into two benches, one on each side of the interior. You can slide out a table between the benches, large enough to be used by two people at the same time.
The best part about the seating area is that it can be turned into a large couch. Amy can add four small panels between the benches to connect them, and then add a cushion on top to create an L-shaped couch. She can even use it to accommodate a guest overnight.
Both benches have hinged tops that can be lifted. The driver-side bench hides a Truma Combi boiler, but the other bench houses something more interesting: a bathroom – yes, you read that right.
You'll find a simple urine-separating toilet that you'll have to remove if you want to shower. It sits on a waterproof, fully-sealed shower pan.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Amy Camps To complete the shower setup, you must attach a curtain to hooks on the ceiling, and connect a sprayer with a hose to the sink's faucet. Then, you can pull it inside the shower curtain, or even use it outside.
The wall panel behind the driver-side bench integrates standard plugs and USB outlets, making the spot perfect for doing some work on the laptop. There's also a control panel for the Truma boiler.
Like most builders, DIYers and professionals alike, Amy used the rear part of the living space to create a bedroom. It boasts a double-sized mattress arranged east to west and two overhead cabinets.
In the gap between the bed and the rear doors, Amy added some more storage space in the form of four compartments.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Amy Camps Finally, we have the garage underneath the bedroom, accessible from both inside and outside the van. It offers additional room to store things and has two boxes on the sides that accommodate the utility systems.
Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are two 115 Ah batteries and a 2,000 W inverter. Three charging sources are available: shore power, solar power , and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 66-liter (17-gallon) freshwater tank and a 50-liter (13-gallon) greywater tank – both are mounted underneath the vehicle. There's also a Shurflo water pump and a Fiamma accumulator. Furthermore, the garage houses a 6-kg (13-lb.) LPG canister in a sealed locker.
All in all, Amy did a fantastic job with this conversion – it did take a while to complete, but all the work was definitely worth it. Not only does it pack the essential creature comforts, but its design is really welcoming and homely.

source_document.body:
Kia announced that 2027 EV6 prices start at about $38,000, or $8,000 more than the new EV3.
2027 Kia EV6 prices and driving range
The 2027 Kia EV6 arrives as a carryover model from last year. After reducing prices on the 2026 model year by $5,000 just a few months ago, the 2027 EV6 remains the same price across all trims.
The base EV6 Light standard-range RWD model starts at $37,900, not including the $1,545 destination fee, which is the same as last year.
Powered by a 63 kWh battery, the standard-range variant offers up to 237 miles of range. Upgrading to the EV6 Light long range RWD model costs an extra $3,300, starting at $41,200, but delivers up to 319 miles of range using a larger 84 kWh battery.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The 84 kWh battery offers up to 319 miles of range in RWD variants, while AWD EV6 models get up to 295 miles. The top-spec EV6 GT-Line AWD has up to 270 miles of range.
2027 Kia EV6 (Source: Kia)
Kia said that with the EV6 MSRP unchanged and the launch of the new EV3, it’s “making EVs more attainable for those who embrace the fully electric lifestyle.”
The 2027 Kia EV3 starts at just $29,890, or about $8,000 less than the EV6. Kia’s entry-level electric SUV is available in five trims: Light, Wind, Land, GT-Line, and GT.
The lowest-priced EV3 Light FWD model uses a 58.3 kWh battery and delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 221 miles.
2027 Kia EV6 | Starting Price * | Driving Range
EV6 Light SR RWD | $37,900 | 237 miles
EV6 Light LR RWD | $41,200 | 319 miles
EV6 Light LR AWD | $45,200 | 295 miles
EV6 Wind RWD | $44,800 | 319 miles
EV6 Wind AWD | $48,800 | 295 miles
EV6 GT-Line RWD | $48,700 | 319 miles
EV6 GT-Line AWD | $53,000 | 270 miles
2027 Kia EV6 prices and driving range (*excluding $1,545 destination fee)
Higher-priced trims, including the Wind, Land, GT-Line, and GT, use a larger 81.4 kWh battery that delivers up to 321 miles of range on a single charge. Like the EV6, the EV3 is also available with front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive powertrain options.
Inside, both the EV6 and EV3 feature Kia’s ccNC infotainment system. The setup includes nearly 30″ of screen space in a curved panoramic display, including dual 12.3″ instrument cluster and central navigation screens, plus a 5″ climate control touchscreen.
2027 Kia EV6 interior (Source: Kia)
Both also include a native NACS port so that you can access Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter.
However, the EV6 uses an 800V architecture, enabling faster charging than the EV3, which uses a 400V system.
2027 Kia EV3 (Source: Kia)
The EV6 can charge from 10% to 80% in about 18 minutes, whereas the EV3 takes about 30 minutes.
The EV6 is also larger and less boxy than the EV3, measuring 184.8″ long, 74″ wide, and 60.8″ tall, with a 114.2″ wheelbase. In comparison, the EV3 is 169.3″ long, 72.8″ wide, and 62″ tall, with a 105.5″ wheelbase.
Which one would you drive? The new EV3, the EV6, or would you go with Kia’s three-row EV9? Let us know in the comments.

1970 Chevrolet Nova Yenko Deuce Flaunts LT1 Power, One of 122 Made
17 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
Don Yenko is primarily known for dropping 427-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) L72 engines in Chevrolet Camaros , but his shop modified other vehicles as well. Yenko actually started out with the Corvair in 1966 and added the Chevelle and Nova to its portfolio in 1969. In 1971-1972, Yenko also built a beefed-up version of the Vega.
Yenko put together two different iterations of the Nova. In 1969, the dealership used the same L72 engine it fitted in the Camaro. Rated at a whopping 425 horsepower, the big-block V8 turned the tiny Nova into a beast. Only 38 of these "Supernovas" were built, and fewer than 10 are known to exist today.
With big-block V8 engines already expensive to insure, Yenko switched to a small-block powerplant in 1970. The dealership's unit of choice was the LT1, a 350-cubic-inch (5.7-liter) V8 usually found in the Camaro Z28 and Chevrolet Corvette. The mill was rated at 360 horsepower; it was more potent than many big-block V8s available at the time.
Nicknamed the Deuce, the 1970 Yenko Nova was produced in notably more units than its 1969 L72 predecessor, but "common" is not the word we're looking for here. That's because only 175 examples rolled out of Don Yenko's shop. They're obviously desirable today and a rare sight out in the open.
If you haven't seen one recently, a Cortez Silver example was recently listed among the lots of Mecum's upcoming Las Vegas 2026 auction. It's in pristine condition, well documented, and equipped with a four-speed manual gearbox. The latter makes this Deuce one of 122 units built with this setup; the other 53 examples have the three-speed automatic gearbox.
This Nova is a true COPO car. Don Yenko utilized COPO sequence 9010 to order the factory-installed LT1 V8 engine. The COPO 9737 process added other features required to turn the Deuce into a proper sports car. The mill mates to a Positraction rear end with a 4.10 ratio, while the car rides on a heavy-duty suspension.
The Nova is obviously loaded with goodies that set it apart from a regular factory model. The list includes an exclusive Hurst shifter, a hood-mounted tach, Yenko-specific alloy wheels, and "sYc" markings ( Yenko Super Car ) on he front seats.
Rotisserie-restored to factory specifications, the Deuce wears the factory-correct Cortez Silver paint, along with black stripes running across the hood, the sides, and the trunk.
The car is absolutely flawless. The paint shines like it was just applied, and the interior doesn't show an inch of wear and tear. The engine? Well, you could basically eat off the air cleaner.
It also comes with a huge folder of valuable paperwork . The car is well documented by the COPO Connection and has a letter of authenticity plus a Yenko Vehicle Verification Certificate. It doesn't get any better than this.
However, there's a catch. The car was actually re-bodied, meaning that it was likely rescued after many years of neglect, and its original sheet metal was consumed by rust. This probably explains why it sold for only $82,500 back in 2009.
But that was a very long time ago, so this Deuce will probably fetch a six-figure sum in 2026. As of this writing, the world's most expensive Deuce Nova is a Fathom Blue example that sold for $230,000. Two more cars fetched a little over $150,000 in recent years. It will go under the hammer on November 14.
